name: Web Application Security
tagline: The full web assessment stack: intercepting proxies, deep content discovery, injection testing, XSS & clickjacking, API security, and OWASP-class bypass tooling — nested by technique.

tools.name: Burp Suite
tools.desc: The de-facto intercepting proxy for manual testing: intercept/edit requests, inspect responses, map the app, and extend via a huge BApp marketplace.
tools.when: Every authorized manual web engagement; the default scratchpad for inspecting and shaping requests to an app in scope.

tools.name: OWASP ZAP
tools.desc: Free and open-source OWASP proxy with automated scanning, fuzzing, DOM spelunking, and a REST API for CI-driven baseline scans.
tools.when: When you need a fully open, scriptable proxy with built-in automation you can drive from a pipeline against a staging app you own.

tools.name: Caido
tools.desc: Lightweight, modern intercepting proxy with a clean UI, fast request replay, and a built-in graph of your target's flow.
tools.when: When you want a slim, single-binary proxy for interception and replay without a heavyweight install footprint.
tools.install: brew tap caido/caido && brew install caido

tools.name: Charles Proxy
tools.desc: Commercial desktop proxy with SSL browsing, bandwidth throttling, and rewrite tools for debugging web traffic.
tools.when: When you want a polished GUI focus on mobile app and local HTTPS traffic you are authorized to inspect.

tools.name: Proxyman
tools.desc: Native macOS proxy with elegant UI, SSL pinning bypass for testing, and script-driven scenarios.
tools.when: When you work primarily on macOS and want a fast proxy with iOS/Android companion apps for your own traffic.

tools.name: ffuf
tools.desc: Extremely fast Go web fuzzer for directories, files, parameters, and vhosts with matchers, filters, and recursion.
tools.when: Anytime you need fast brute-force discovery of paths or parameters against a target you are authorized to test.

tools.name: gobuster
tools.desc: Simple multi-purpose fuzzer for directories, DNS subdomains, and virtual hosts using wordlists.
tools.when: When you want a lightweight, easy-to-script brute forcer for your scoped discovery phase.

tools.name: feroxbuster
tools.desc: Fast recursive content discovery fuzzer in Rust that automatically scans directories it finds.
tools.when: When you want recursion plus auto-rescanning of discovered directories out of the box.

tools.name: dirsearch
tools.desc: Mature Python path scanner with threading, proxy support, and rich status-code filters.
tools.when: When a straightforward, cross-platform Python scanner with many wordlist and output options is all you need.

tools.name: wfuzz
tools.desc: Flexible Python fuzzer for web content and parameters with rich payload/encoding options and multi-position iteration.
tools.when: When you need fine-grained iteration over multiple payload positions and encoding filters in your tests.

tools.name: Arjun
tools.desc: Finds hidden HTTP parameters in URLs and header values using a large wordlist and heuristics.
tools.when: When you want to discover undocumented parameters an API or page accepts on a target in scope.

tools.name: x8
tools.desc: Fast Go-based hidden parameter fuzzer with configurable detection heuristics and concurrency.
tools.when: When you need a fast single-binary parameter miner that integrates into shell pipelines.

tools.name: Param Miner
tools.desc: Burp Suite extension that guesses hidden parameters, headers, and cookies on both base requests and reflected points.
tools.when: When you are already in Burp and want passive parameter guessing while you manually explore in scope.
tools.install: Install 'Param Miner' from the Burp BApp Store

tools.name: ParamSpider
tools.desc: Scrapes parameters from Wayback, Common Crawl, and more to compile endpoint lists for later fuzzing.
tools.when: When you want to bulk-collect parameter-bearing URLs from archives to feed subsequent testing.

tools.name: ffuf
tools.desc: Can brute-force virtual hosts by fuzzing the Host header and matching on distinct response sizes.
tools.when: When you want to enumerate in-scope virtual hosts behind a shared IP or reverse proxy.

tools.name: gobuster
tools.desc: Supports a dedicated vhost mode that fuzzes the Host header against a known target.
tools.when: When you prefer a single simple binary for a quick virtual-host sweep on authorized targets.

tools.name: SecLists
tools.desc: The community standard collection of wordlists for discovery, fuzzing, injection, usernames, passwords, and more.
tools.when: When you need a broad, trustworthy baseline wordlist for any scoped fuzzing activity.

tools.name: PayloadsAllTheThings
tools.desc: Categorized payloads and cheat sheets for every injection class, from RCE to SSTI to SSRF.
tools.when: When you need a quick, in-context payload reference while crafting manual tests.

tools.name: Assetnote Wordlists
tools.desc: Industry-derived wordlists built from massive real-world indexed datasets, including API parameter lists.
tools.when: When baseline wordlists miss and you need high-quality lists for API and content discovery.

tools.name: raft (Rapid Fire Threads)
tools.desc: Classic raft wordlists (small/medium/large) for directories and files, maintained inside SecLists.
tools.when: When you want quick, proven-size wordlists tuned to file and directory names without noise.

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.desc: The reference automated SQLi tool: detects and exploits injection in GET/POST/headers, enumerates DBMSes, and dumps data on authorized targets.
tools.when: When a parameter looks injectable and you want thorough detection, DB fingerprinting, safe limits, and batch modes.

tools.name: jSQL Injection
tools.desc: Java GUI tool for automated SQLi detection and exploitation with SQLi and NoSQL/path-style payloads.
tools.when: When you want a desktop GUI over automated SQLi rather than a CLI-only flow on your scoped targets.

tools.name: NoSQLMap
tools.desc: Automated testing tool for NoSQL databases (MongoDB, CouchDB) injection and misconfiguration.
tools.when: When the backend is NoSQL and you need injection-point discovery against an app in scope.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/codingo/NoSQLMap && pip install -r NoSQLMap/requirements.txt

tools.name: Commix
tools.desc: Automated OS command injection detection and exploitation with support for many injection techniques and filter bypasses.
tools.when: When you suspect command injection in a parameter or header and want an automated detector on authorized targets.

tools.name: tplmap
tools.desc: Detects and exploits server-side template injection across engines (Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker, etc.).
tools.when: When an app renders user input inside templates and you need to confirm SSTI on a scope-authorized target.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/epinna/tplmap && pip install -r tplmap/requirements.txt

tools.name: SSTImap
tools.desc: Actively maintained fork/rewrite of tplmap for SSTI detection and exploitation across web template engines.
tools.when: When tplmap is unmaintained and you want current engine payload support for your authorized tests.

tools.name: webbreach
tools.desc: OWASP Top-10 attack engine with built-in localhost vulnerable targets and an AI-guided scan queue — safe web exploitation practice.
tools.when: Practicing web app attacks without touching the internet.

tools.name: Dalfox
tools.desc: Fast XSS scanner with parameter analysis, payload generation, detection of reflection points, and CI-friendly output.
tools.when: When you want to automate XSS discovery against endpoint lists on authorized targets and pipeline results.

tools.name: XSStrike
tools.desc: XSS detection suite with payload crafting, bruteforce, and WAF/filter-detection heuristics.
tools.when: When you need sophisticated payload crafting and WAF detection for manual XSS validation in your tests.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/s0md3v/XSStrike && pip install -r XSStrike/requirements.txt

tools.name: xsser
tools.desc: Long-standing XSS scanner with encoding/obfuscation bypasses, DORCE, and crawler support.
tools.when: When you want a classic CLI scanner with many encoding bypass options against in-scope pages.

tools.name: XSS Hunter Express
tools.desc: Self-hostable platform that proves XSS via injected payload probes sending interactive callback notifications.
tools.when: When you need persistent, hosted OOB XSS payloads that report callbacks during a longer engagement.

tools.name: quickjack
tools.desc: Point-and-click PoC generator for advanced clickjacking and frame slicing attacks with generated HTML snippets.
tools.when: When you found a frameable page without X-Frame-Options/CSP frame-ancestors and need a PoC to demonstrate it.
tools.install: Open the hosted generator at https://samy.pl/quickjack/quickjack.html

tools.name: ClickjackPoc
tools.desc: Minimal browser-extension/POC helper for generating HTML clickjacking proofs quickly.
tools.when: When you want a fast, scriptable way to produce clickjacking PoC HTML for reports.

tools.name: Postman
tools.desc: API client and collection runner for crafting, saving, and automating HTTP requests against services under test.
tools.when: When you need organized collections, environments, and simple automation to reason about an API's behavior.

tools.name: Bruno
tools.desc: Open-source, offline-first API client using plain-text collections you can version in git.
tools.when: When you want API collections stored as data you can review and diff in code review.

tools.name: HTTPie
tools.desc: User-friendly command-line HTTP client with readable, colorful output for quick manual requests.
tools.when: For fast ad-hoc requests in a terminal during investigation without a heavyweight GUI.

tools.name: mitmproxy
tools.desc: Interactive man-in-the-middle proxy with a powerful scriptable (Python) add-on API for request shaping and inspection.
tools.when: When you need programmatic control over intercepted API and app traffic (rewrite, capture, fuzz) in your tests.

tools.name: HTTP Toolkit
tools.desc: GUI proxy for intercepting, inspecting, and mocking HTTP(S) traffic from browsers, Android, and server processes.
tools.when: When you want zero-config TLS interception and a friendly UI for debugging your own or in-scope traffic.

tools.name: schemathesis
tools.desc: Property-based testing for OpenAPI/GraphQL schemas that generates edge-case requests to uncover 5xx and contract violations.
tools.when: When an API publishes an OpenAPI spec and you want automated schema-driven testing in CI.

tools.name: kiterunner
tools.desc: Assetnote's fast API endpoint and route discovery scanner optimized against massive route wordlists.
tools.when: When you want to expose undocumented API routes and endpoints a spec won't tell you about.

tools.name: byp4xx
tools.desc: Rapid 403/40x bypasser that tries path normalization, header tricks, and encoding variations against protected endpoints.
tools.when: When an API path returns 403 solely due to WAF/path rules and you want to test authorized bypass vectors.

tools.name: nomore403
tools.desc: Go tool that scans a list of 403 URLs and tries common bypass techniques to reveal hidden content.
tools.when: When you have many blocked URLs from crawling and want an automated sweep across bypass techniques.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/devploit/nomore403 && sudo python3 nomore403.py -u https://target/

tools.name: jwt_tool
tools.desc: Audits JSON Web Tokens: signature verification, algorithm confusion, known CVE checks, and secret brute-forcing.
tools.when: When an app uses JWTs and you need to inspect claims, check alg:none/confusion, and validate signing secrets.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/ticarpi/jwt_tool && cd jwt_tool && pip install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: JWT Editor
tools.desc: Official Burp extension to encode, decode, forge, and tamper with JWTs including alg confusion and kid injection.
tools.when: When you are already inside Burp and want intercept-time JWT tampering on requests in scope.
tools.install: Install 'JWT Editor' from the Burp BApp Store

tools.name: JWT4B
tools.desc: Burp Suite tab extension that decodes, validates, and brute-forces JWT signatures with attack templates.
tools.when: When you prefer a dedicated Burp tab for JWT analysis and signature brute-forcing during a test.

tools.name: SSRFmap
tools.desc: Automates SSRF discovery and exploitation including file reads, port scans, and protocol-based attacks.
tools.when: When a URL/parameter fetches remote content and you want to confirm and demo SSRF impact in scope.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/swisskyrepo/SSRFmap && pip install -r SSRFmap/requirements.txt

tools.name: Gopherus
tools.desc: Generates Gopher payloads to attack MySQL, Redis, SMTP, and more from SSRF-capable endpoints.
tools.when: When you have an SSRF that reaches internal services and need gopher payload generation for exploitation.

tools.name: interactsh
tools.desc: Open-source Out-of-Band interaction server with client that catches DNS/HTTP/SMTP callbacks for SSRF and OAST.
tools.when: When you want self-hosted or public OOB callbacks to confirm blind SSRF, XSS, or injection in authorized tests.

tools.name: smuggler
tools.desc: Detects HTTP request smuggling variants (CL.TE, TE.CL, TE.TE obfuscation) against proxy/backend parsing mismatches.
tools.when: When a stack splits differently between proxies and back-ends and you want to test smuggling scenarios in scope.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/defparam/smuggler && python3 smuggler.py regex.txt urls.txt

tools.name: HTTP Request Smuggler
tools.desc: Official PortSwigger extension automating CL.TE / TE.CL / TE.TE smuggling detection and exploit generation.
tools.when: When you are inside Burp and want integrated smuggling detection with guided payload confirmation.
tools.install: Install 'HTTP Request Smuggler' from the Burp BApp Store

tools.name: testssl.sh
tools.desc: Free TLS/SSL audit CLI that checks ciphers, protocols, certificate chains, BEAST/POODLE/Heartbleed-family issues, and client-auth (mTLS) settings.
tools.when: When you need a thorough, fork-friendly TLS configuration audit of an endpoint you are authorized to test.

tools.name: sslyze
tools.desc: Fast Python TLS scanner analyzing SSL configs, supported ciphers, and certificate details, scriptable for CI.
tools.when: When you need structured, machine-readable TLS scan output across many hosts in your own infrastructure.

tools.name: CSP Evaluator
tools.desc: Google's hosted query engine that flags weak Content-Security-Policy directives that allow XSS to slip through.
tools.when: When the target sends a CSP and you want to quickly grade its effectiveness and find bypassable directives.
tools.install: Open the hosted checker at https://csp-evaluator.withgoogle.com

tools.name: SecurityHeaders.com
tools.desc: Scans a URL's response headers against the OWASP Secure Headers Project and scores the hardening state.
tools.when: When you want an instant, shareable header hardening report for a site you own or administer.

tools.name: headers.dev
tools.desc: Simple API/website that returns all response headers of a URL for quick inspection from the terminal.
tools.when: When you want a fast, no-install way to pull and eyeball a target's response headers.

tools.name: httpx
tools.desc: ProjectDiscovery's fast HTTP toolkit that fingerprints hosts, technologies, status codes, and response headers at scale.
tools.when: When you need to bulk-collect status codes, headers, and tech fingerprints across hundreds of in-scope hosts.
